definition: In this historical source, a simple tone is a basic tone contrasted with a compound tone. The entry notes that some writers treated it as the same as a simple clang, although it also argues that clang is more strictly the term for a musical note made up of a fundamental tone and its overtones.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Clang; pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define “simple tone” as a “basic tone contrasted with a compound tone”; it only states that a “simple clang” is often identified with the “simple TONE,” while discussing “tone” vs “clang,” without providing the requested contrast definition for “simple tone.”

The definition’s claim about “some writers treated it as the same as a simple clang” is only partially supported: the packet says “The simple clang is often identified with the simple TONE (q.v.),” but does not identify which writers or the nature of that treatment beyond that general statement.

The remainder about “clang” being more strictly a musical note made of fundamental tone and overtones is supported in the packet, but the overall definition includes additional substantive claims not fully grounded in the provided text.
